outcome: Cause-specific mortality (cancer, cardiovascular disease, other diseases)
cohort: The study comprised 16,962 adult American women from a nationally representative cohort with available self-reported parity data and survival follow-up.
finding: Nulliparous women exhibited a higher risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality compared to parous women, with depression partially mediating the association between parity and women's all-cause mortality and mortality from other diseases.
cross-section timing: Data for baseline characteristics was collected from seven cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) spanning 2005-2018.
